title: Severe audio crackling/distortion using Realtek High Definition Audio with high sampling rates and surround sound
body: ### Tested versions - Reproducible in v4.4.1.stable.mono.official.49a5bc7b6 ### System information Windows 10, Vulkan 1.4.303 (Forward+), NVIDIA GeForce GTX 980, Realtek High Definition Audio ### Issue description In Thrive, a Godot-based game, I have severe issues with audio crackling/distortion while the game is running (i.e., not paused). See/hear the video below. https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/48f147e8-ce0e-4656-8edf-af0ed469684d I have reported the issue at https://github.com/Revolutionary-Games/Thrive/issues/5050#issuecomment-3113068622, where it was suggested to also report it as a Godot issue. ### Steps to reproduce This issue happens specifically with a Realtek High Definition Audio device on Windows 10 using the Realtek HD Audio manager driver software with many sound channels and a high sampling rate. I normally use 7.1 Surround Sound together with 24 Bit, 192000 Hz as the default sampling format used in shared mode. Using 5.1 Surround Sound decreases the crackling a bit, and Stereo fixes it almost entirely. However, the main culprit appears to be the shared mode sampling rate. Reducing it to 96000 Hz or 48000 Hz fixes the crackling entirely also with 7.1 Surround Sound.
